cues.en: And for this I got another new project for you which you find attached.
Now, this is not a svelte project, but a separate project.
Of course, implicitly it therefore also is a svelte project.
And indeed in the package.json file you will find svelte as a dependency, but you also find Sapper.
Now, Sapper does two things.
It adds a nodejs server and it forces a certain folder structure on you that allows you to map svelte
components to certain paths in the URL.
Now, in this project, which you find attached in the source folder, you'll actually find two folders
components and routes.
Now actually, both folders contain svelte components, but the components in the routes folder are
mapped to paths in the URL.
The components in the components folder are simply embedded into other components.
These are not reachable through URLs.
Now the components and the routes folder are mapped to the paths which fit their file names.
So for example about would be reached on your domain.com slash about index would be reached on just
your domain slash nothing.
The error and layout components are special components too, which I'll come back in the blog folder.
The components in there would be reached on your domain slash blog, and then you have this underscore
thing which is also special.
And I'll come back to this too.
Then we also have client and server JS.
Client JS is some code that runs when the app is loaded on the client for the first time.
Here, it's importing something which is automatically generated by Sapper, which simply starts the
app, which means it takes the Pre-rendered page from Sapper and connects that to the client side app,
which now is starting.
And in Server.js that is the NodeJS server, which in the end does all the heavy lifting.
It connects the sapper middleware, which then in turn is responsible for server side rendering and
so on.
Now you also get a service worker out of the box that is a feature which can help you with offline caching
of your app.
I'll not dive into it here.
You can have a look at my progressive web app course if you want to learn more about service workers
and the template file that in the end is the index.html file from before.
It is that single page that is shipped back to the client.
But since that now is pre-rendered on the server, it has separate entry points here for sapper where
it will render content that needs to be rendered for a specific svelte page and component, for example
the main content, but also the head section and so on.
You don't need to change anything here.
You interact with that template from inside your svelte root components.
So that's the general structure.
Let's now dive deeper into these routes and understand how that works and how we can actually see what
this project gives us.
